chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying about a man who had performed the dawn prayer, then when he sat in the two rakʿahs before reciting the tashahhud, he had a nosebleed:
He said: Let him go out, wash his nose, then return and complete his salat (prayer).
He said: Indeed, the end of the salat (prayer) is the taslīm.

His statement عليه السلام, “Indeed, the end of the salat (prayer) is the taslīm,” is to be understood as referring to merit and perfection. As for completing the salat (prayer), that is indispensable, because part of its completion is bringing the two testimonies and the salat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, as we have explained.

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: the closing salutation of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man about whom the legal ruling is being discussed
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of the prayer
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies recited in the tashahhud
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), which he is instructed to complete
key_terms.فَلْيَغْسِلْ: let him wash, referring here to cleansing the nose from blood

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he gets a nosebleed before tashahhud in the dawn prayer, and is taslīm obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one who experiences a nosebleed during the final sitting of the dawn prayer before tashahhud. He is instructed to wash the blood and then return to complete the prayer, while the statement that taslīm is the end of prayer is understood here in the sense of perfection and completion rather than as an absolute obligation.
